chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray the two rak'at of the obligatory Tawaf behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham), and Allah the Exalted said, 'And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer.' He then traveled (left the area), so he said, 'If he had traveled, I would not make it difficult for him nor order him to return, but he should pray wherever he remembers.'
And that which indicates that whoever for whom it is not difficult is obliged to return to it and pray at the Maqam is what has been narrated:

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two obligatory rak'at of prayer performed during Tawaf
key_terms.لَا أَشُقُّ عَلَيْهِ: I do not make it difficult/hard for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the two rak'at behind Maqam Ibrahim during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *la yukallifu nafsatan illa wusaha* (God imposes no burden beyond capacity) in the context of Tawaf prayers, distinguishing between obligatory return (*lazim*) and recommended return based on physical hardship. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the Quranic command to take the Maqam as a place of prayer establishes its spiritual significance, the legal obligation to return is contingent upon the pilgrim's ability to do so without undue difficulty. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual precision with practical ease for the worshipper.
